title: Tenant traffic‑shielded phased API promotion for private control plane
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Implement a phased promotion workflow for private control plane API server versions that uses tenant-aware traffic shields (lightweight routing fences) to route small cohorts to the new version, validate health & correctness, and then progressively expand. This complements existing canary semantics by adding tenant isolation, terraform module flags, and in‑flight KV cache compatibility checks specific to our private (VPC) deployments.
background: We frequently need to roll control plane versions into customers' VPCs with minimal disruption. Current canary approaches exercise small percentages of traffic but don't provide tenant-level isolation or a repeatable Terraform hook to opt cohorts into new control plane behaviors. Several incidents showed latent incompatibilities when tenant-specific config or operator CRDs changed between versions.
goals: Provide tenant-level canary gating so we can validate entire tenant workloads (not just % of requests)
Add Terraform flags and module outputs to allow infra teams to opt a tenant into a version cohort
Instrument richer health checks (API + CRD contract checks + KV cache warmup) before expanding
Enable automated rollback and postmortem hooks when regressions cross thresholds
success_metrics: Reduce post-upgrade incidents for private control plane by 60% for tenants in staged rollouts
Time-to-detect regressions in canaries < 10 minutes via alerting rules
Ability to promote from 1 tenant -> 10 tenants within 2 hours if all health gates pass
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes `promote_cohort` boolean and `cohort_id` string outputs
Routing layer supports `traffic_shield: <cohort_id>` header-based steering for private control planes
Health checks include: APIserver readiness, CRD schema conformance probe, KV cache warmup and response consistency checks
Automated rollback trigger fires when composite health score < 0.9 for 5m
Playbook documented in Confluence with runbook steps and runbook links included in the ticket
scope_in_scope: Terraform module changes for private control plane stack (module: private/controlplane)
Routing/edge update to add header-based tenant shields (control-plane router component)
Health probes implemented in operator and control plane agent
Rollout automation to sequence cohorts and emit telemetry
out_of_scope: Changes to public hosted API upgrade mechanisms
design_summary: Add a lightweight 'traffic_shield' concept that attaches a stable cohort identifier to tenant metadata. The router understands the shield and can route only traffic originating from that tenant to the promoted control plane variant. Terraform will allow operators to define cohorts by setting `cohort_id` on tenant infra stacks. Promotion is orchestrated by a controller that flips route weights for tenant namespaces and runs a staged health-check pipeline before widening the cohort. Health checks are composite: API liveness, operator CRD conformance, KV prefix checksum validation, and end-to-end reconcile smoke tests.
terraform_changes: module/private/route: expose `traffic_shield` output consumed by router provisioning
Add `cohort_state` remote state object to track which tenants are in which cohort
canary_strategy: Tenant cohort progression: stage 0 = shadow (no traffic), stage 1 = single tenant + internal test traffic, stage 2 = 5 tenants, stage 3 = 20 tenants, stage 4 = full promotion. Each stage requires passing the composite health checks and manual signoff for stages 2+. Early stages auto-advance when all checks are green for 30 minutes; later stages require PM approval. Rollouts include a configurable 'blast radius' cap per promotion window.
health_checks: API readiness probe: must return 200 for control-plane /healthz for 3 consecutive checks
CRD conformance: validate a sample set of CRs using `kubectl`-like schema verification
KV cache warmup: ensure cached prefixes used by tenant return identical checksums after warmup (within X ms)
Reconcile smoke tests: create+delete a sample resource through operator and verify final state
Latency regression check: 95th percentile API latency not increased by > 30% vs baseline
observability: Dashboards: `private.upgrades.cohort_overview`, `private.upgrades.health_rollup`, and per-tenant latency/cost breakdowns. Alerts: composite health score alert, cohort regression alert, and rollout-stalled alert. Logs: enrich control-plane logs with `cohort_id` and `promoted_version` fields. Traces: sample request traces from promoted tenants for end-to-end latency analysis.
rollback_criteria: Rollback immediately if any of: composite health score < 0.9 for 5 minutes, end-to-end reconcile failures > 1% of sampled requests in a 10 minute window, or manual abort from oncall. Rollback steps: flip tenant routing back to previous variant, invalidate promoted version in state, and run failure collection job that captures diagnostics and uploads to S3 for postmortem.
